changes.title: Use the published analyzer in the skill and ship its guides
changes.body:
## Summary

A copied OUCH skill required a built checkout, and the npm package omitted the guides its README linked to. The skill now uses the published analyzer and can open the matching docs offline.

```text
Project or workspace has ouch4ts → use the installed version
Analyzer missing                 → ask before installing or running npx once
Need the full CLI reference     → open the local path printed by --help
```

The release check requires all six analyzer guides in the tarball. The 0BSD skill stays separate from the MIT package. The repository instructions also direct agents to fetch origin and start new work on a branch based on origin/main.

## Evidence

- A workspace used its installed 0.1.0 with 0.1.1 already in npm's cache. A one-off report using existing coverage added only `.metrics/ouch.json`.
- Installed the new tarball locally, in a workspace, and with offline `npx`. Each invocation found its CLI reference. All 17 relative links and anchors in the packaged docs resolved.
- Typecheck, build, and all 371 tests passed. The release check rejected both a missing coverage guide and an unexpected contributor guide.

## Merge danger

Merging with `release:patch` triggers an npm preview. The separate rolling release PR controls stable publication.

Implements [Switch the BSD0 skill to the published npm analyzer](https://github.com/dumptruckman/ouch4ts/issues/13).
changes.head: jwood/package-analyzer-docs
